rci.method: RC = (current - baseline mean) / S_diff, S_diff = sqrt(2) x SEM, SEM = SD x sqrt(1 - r), SD = sample SD (n - 1) of the crewmember's own baseline.

source.arithmetic: z with 2 x (1 - Phi(z)) = 0.001 gives z = 3.2905, printed as 3.29

source.rationale: Stricter than the conventional 0.05 (z = 1.96) that Jacobson & Truax used, because LANDFALL tests many indicators every day; the expected false-alarm rate is printed next to every personal finding.
Seven baseline days is the fewest we accept for a sample SD; below that the finding is insufficient_data.
Two weeks of the crewmember's own data, long enough to span weekday/weekend schedule differences.

rci.caveat: The 3.29 criterion is nominally two-tailed p < .001. Jacobson & Truax built S_diff from a reference-group SD and a published test-retest r. LANDFALL uses the crewmember's own baseline SD, which already contains the day-to-day error, so the realized false-alarm rate is higher than the nominal one. Treat the printed rate as a lower bound.

source.rationale: Borrowed from the 10-min PVT. We found no published test-retest value for the 3-min PVT-B, so applying 0.8, the lower bound, to it is our assumption.
